summary_text: The user has demonstrated a stable preference for Amul brand, specifically Pasteurised Salted Butter, supported by purchases across multiple months (Feb, Apr, May, Jun, Jul 2026). The most robust evidence comes from April 2026, where two independent weekend afternoon purchases established a medium-confidence stable preference for both the brand and the salted butter variant. While other months show single observations of the same product (often 100g or 200g packs), the repetition of Amul salted butter across five distinct months confirms it as the primary category anchor. Timing varies (morning, afternoon, evening, weekday, weekend), preventing a single high-confidence daypart pattern, though morning activity aligns with population baselines.

substitution_text: Amul Pasteurised Salted Butter is the established staple. No evidence of substitution to other brands or margarine types was observed; the user consistently returns to this specific product line.
uncertainty_text: While the brand and product type (salted butter) are stable, the specific pack size (100g vs 200g) and daypart timing are not consistently repeated enough to establish high-confidence stable preferences. The user buys this product across different times of day (morning, afternoon, evening) and days (weekday, weekend), suggesting flexibility in timing rather than a rigid routine. It is unknown if the user would accept unsalted butter or other brands if Amul salted butter were unavailable.
